argument:
Tenaga's extracted cash verifies investment and dividend capacity, but RM1.8018bn after specified financing and leases only narrowly exceeded RM1.6322bn dividends. That leaves limited cushion alongside RM60.936bn borrowings and RM31.198bn leases. Cash/deposits include restricted or longer-tenor balances, so they are not all immediately available for debt service.

The bull's modest H1 operating-profit increase preserves utility resilience. Nonetheless Q2 operating margin contracted and owners earnings fell; FX explains part, not all, of that pressure. A 16.83x multiple and 3.85% reported yield require regulated returns and collection timing to sustain coverage through heavy grid investment. Cash strength makes ownership plausible but cannot prove every capex project earns its cost. Weak technicals add entry caution without asserting an unobserved tariff shock or funding crisis.
key_points: Dividend coverage after financing and leases is narrow.
Large separate lease and borrowing burdens remain.
Margin and regulatory cash timing qualify utility resilience.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull demonstrates coverage rather than an extraction gap, but only narrowly: RM1.8018bn surplus versus RM1.6322bn dividends. Large obligations and contracted margin leave little room for weaker regulated cash conversion.
